about: The limits studio/scripts/perf-check.mjs holds a release build to. Every number is a measure and its basis: a time is the median documented in docs/studio-performance.md, held to the rule named by its group; a growth per switch is held to an absolute tolerance. To change one, edit it with the new table from a run, in the PR that makes the code faster (docs/studio-performance.md, 'Refreshing the limits').

time.basis: twice the documented median, and at least 50 ms: three frames at 60 Hz, below which a switch is not felt as slow and the spread of a run of three repetitions is larger than the median

command.basis: twice the documented median of a command's own run, no floor: a command that was moved off the window's main thread is held to its new time

count.basis: twice the documented count, which a closed page may hold once and not grow

growth.basis: nothing gained per page switch from switch 50 to 200 (documented: 0.0 DOM nodes, 0.00 listeners), within a tolerance of less than one node and a tenth of a listener per switch: a leak of one node per switch is 150 nodes over those switches, a listener a tenth as often is 15

pages.about: Switching pages (docs/studio-performance.md, 'Switching pages'): documented medians in ms, the first frame and the settled time, in a workspace of 34 jobs and 204 runs.

tabs.about: Switching a component's tabs ('Switching a component's tabs'): documented medians in ms over the all-pass ring, the Mach–Zehnder modulator and the waveguide.

loads.about: The first click on Components in a fresh launch, once the window has booted ('The change', the 'after' columns), in ms from the click: the list's names shown, and settled. 'empty' is an empty workspace, 'seeded' the one of 34 jobs and 204 runs.

commands.about: The commands of the first click on Components in the seeded workspace ('home' off the main thread, and read once): the median of a command's own run, in ms, and where it runs.

heap.about: After 200 page switches, a garbage collection after each 50 ('Nothing left behind when a page closes'). Growth is per switch from switch 50 to 200; the detached nodes still held are Svelte's templates, kept once each.

contexts.about: WebGL contexts after each of three rounds of page switches and of opening components ('Contexts released when a view closes'): the browser evicts none, and none on the page is lost.
